name: Marc Ward
life: “I still remember returning from prison to a kitchen with unfamiliar cups.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the bank steps, where Marc takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I shared his flat after prison. The tab includes meals for men whose first paycheck hadn't come.
appearance: Marc has a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. When somebody else has the floor, Marc gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Marc treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To recognize the meals bought for new arrivals after prison.
family: Terry Acosta is Marc’s half-sibling. Marc sets the time to leave. Terry picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The upstairs piano*, Terry says, “My father scratched the piano name off after the creditors came.”
connections: Faye Daniels. They discuss who gets to direct the memorial money after shared prison housing ends.

reactions.situation: The deli is asked to publish the whole tab
reactions.response: Marc asks who owns the personal information on the tab before any of it leaves the counter.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Marc moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.

reactions.response: Marc changes the plan openly and takes responsibility for the delay.
